hlido_opinion.headline: A local-first Markdown editor with a bundled MCP server, so Claude Code / Cursor / Codex can drive your notes vault directly — a clean take on "agent-native" note-taking, with BYOK across 14 providers.
hlido_opinion.body: SoloMD's pitch — "the editor where agents live" — is more precise than the usual AI-note-app copy. It is a small (~15 MB), MIT-licensed, Tauri-based Markdown editor that keeps your files as plain .md on disk, and its differentiator is a bundled MCP server: the same vault is editable by you in the app and drivable from outside by Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex over Model Context Protocol. That local-first, plain-files posture matters for lock-in — your data isn't trapped in a proprietary store — and the BYOK model across 14 providers means you aren't captive to one LLM vendor. The repository shows genuine maintenance (tagged releases, download counters, extensive multi-language READMEs, a public security page). The honest caveats: this is a single-author desktop app in a category crowded by Obsidian (with its own thriving plugin and MCP ecosystem), and the "scheduled recipes" / agent-surface features are the newest and least battle-tested part of the story. For someone who wants their notes to be first-class agent-addressable without leaving a local editor, it's a thoughtful, low-lock-in choice.

tier_rationale: STEADY reflects a well-maintained, MIT-licensed, local-first project with real release cadence, community download traction, and a coherent agent-native design (bundled MCP, BYOK). Not higher because it is a public-surface + repo-health assessment (medium confidence), it competes against the deeply entrenched Obsidian, and its agent-recipe features are recent and unproven at Hlido's evidence tier.
what_it_does_well: Local-first, plain .md files — low lock-in and portable data
Bundled MCP server lets external agents (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) drive the same vault
BYOK across 14 providers — no single-LLM captivity
Small footprint (~15 MB, Tauri) and MIT-licensed
Strong maintenance signals: tagged releases, download counters, published security page, extensive localisation
what_it_fails_at: Competes head-on with Obsidian, which already has a mature plugin + MCP ecosystem
Appears to be a single-maintainer project — bus-factor and long-term support risk
The scheduled-recipes / agent-surface features are the newest and least proven part
No public live demo Hlido could exercise; assessment is of the repo and stated behaviour
Desktop-app distribution means no browsable web trial before download
best_for: Note-takers who want their vault to be directly addressable by coding agents via MCP
Users who value local-first, plain-Markdown storage and low lock-in
People who want to switch LLM providers freely (BYOK)
Lightweight-editor fans who find full IDE-style tools overkill
not_recommended_for: Teams already deeply invested in Obsidian's plugin ecosystem with little reason to move
Buyers who need enterprise support guarantees behind a single-maintainer project
Users wanting a hosted, cross-device-sync-first notes service (this is local-first)
Anyone needing a web trial before installing a desktop binary
red_flags: Single-maintainer open-source project: verify release cadence and issue responsiveness before depending on it for critical workflows.
